name: Cheat codes
goalName: Implement an easy way to add cheats for debugging
goal: While testing, especially with the enemy's shooting scripts added, I either have to disable the scripts or dodge the attacks. It would be easier to have cheats easily accessible for testing purposes.

approach.text: The experts from the first internship gave me code for the project to work with. To add cheats to my own project, I looked at how their code worked and tried replicating it. I understood how the UI was created.

The given code was very complicated, so I decided to try finishing it myself. The execution of the UI was different than I expected, as the OnGUI method is invoked like the Update method. Especially the toggle gave me some trouble.

The following source gave me the idea of having the values of the toggles in a seperate list outside the OnGUI method: <<source How does GUI.Toggle work? - Unity Answers. (07-12-2012). https://answers.unity.com/questions/360635/strange-guitoggle-behavior.html>>. Using my previous knowledge of reflection and answers from other developers, I managed to create cheat codes in a flexible manner. First, I got a list of the classes in the namespace containing all cheat codes using the source <<source How can I get all classes within a namespace? (07-03-2018). Stack Overflow. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/949246/how-can-i-get-all-classes-within-a-namespace>>. The following source helped me get the static Cheat instance from the class to add to the list of cheats: <<source Get value of a public static field via reflection. (05-05-2011). Stack Overflow. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5898385/get-value-of-a-public-static-field-via-reflection>>.

normalLearnings: I learned how to create Unity editor windows.
I learned how to add controls and UI elements to a custom window.
I learned how to use reflection to get a list of classes.
